note: I read the draft end-to-end, tracing its structure literally. The headline result: the round-3 re-emission's own mechanical note ("ONE North Star copy, ONE copy of each phase, launch-surface item 2 restored intact") is falsified by the artifact itself. The corruption the Synthesizer ruled not-lockable in round 2 is still present — now recursively. My angle-specific (frustrated-UX) findings follow the structural ones.

findings.section: whole document (Phase 3 launch-surface item 2; changelog item 1; phase overview)
findings.criterion: all six — the master plan is the lockable artifact; a corrupted plan cannot verify any criterion
findings.message: The re-emission claims the corruption is fixed; it is not — it has gotten worse. Concretely: (a) Phase 3's launch-surface item 2 still reads "envelope-measured today (real `" followed by an ENTIRE embedded copy of the round-2 draft — which itself contains, at its own item 2, a second-level embedding of the round-3 document, i.e. the corruption is now RECURSIVE. (b) The North Star appears at least three times (outer copy, embedded-draft copy, embedded-round-3 copy), directly contradicting "Exactly ONE North Star copy remains." (c) The embedded copies retain the double numbering ("Phase 1 — Phase 0", "Phase 2 — Phase 1"…) the changelog claims was collapsed. (d) The changelog's own item 1 is truncated by the same bug mid-sentence ("restored intact (`job_runner`: real envelope `" → another full document). (e) Raw patch syntax (`>>>>`, `<<<<`, `====`) sits verbatim in the phase-overview section — the reviser emitted unapplied search/replace blocks into the artifact instead of applying them. Diagnose the mechanism, not just the symptom: every corruption site is the literal `$` character inside backticks ("real envelope `$`") — some substitution step is expanding `$`-in-backticks into the whole document. Until the reviser re-emits from scratch (not by patching the corrupted text) and the `$` glyph survives, this plan cannot lock.

findings.criterion: criteria 2, 4, 5, 6 — pricing, surfaces, backfill, and ship phases exist only inside a corrupted embedding
findings.message: Trace the outer document's own heading sequence: Phase overview → Phase 0 → Phase 1 → Phase 2 → Phase 3 → [embedded foreign document opens mid-item-2] → …the outer document then resumes only at the fragment "distinct per Stage-0 decision 3, plus the pin)" and the changelog. The standalone top-level "Phase 4 — Pricing engine", "Phase 5 — Surfaces", "Phase 6 — Historical backfill", and "Phase 7 — Ship" sections appear ONLY inside the embedded round-2 copy (where Phase 4 appears twice under two different titles: "Phase 4 — Phase 3 — Forward swarm…" and "Phase 4 — Pricing engine…"). A builder (Foreman) parsing top-level headings of the authoritative document gets a plan that ends at Phase 3. Criteria 5 (dollars), 2 (surfaces), 6 (counting), and 4 (backfill) have no authoritative phase text at the document's top level. This is not a formatting nit — it is the difference between an 8-phase plan and a 4-phase plan depending on which nesting level you believe.

findings.criterion: all — an inaccurate self-report on the lock artifact defeats the convergence loop itself
findings.message: The changelog asserts, in past tense and as fact: "The full second copy … is excised; the double phase numbering … is collapsed; … launch-table item 2 is restored intact … Exactly ONE North Star copy remains." Every one of those statements is false of the emitted artifact (see Findings 1–2). For a plan whose entire theme is honest, verifiable claims ("never a fabricated 0", "vacuous-GREEN is a real failure mode here"), the plan document itself shipping a vacuous-GREEN changelog is disqualifying. The reviser's changelog to the Sharks was also 18 lines of "Applied a search/replace patch" with zero content — the review loop cannot converge when the revision record carries no information and the summary claims are unverified. Requirement: the next revision must be a from-scratch re-emission, and its changelog must be checkable against the artifact (e.g., "grep count of '# NORTH STAR' == 1").

findings.section: Phase 2 deferrals vs Phase 3 walk-through vs North Star Statement
findings.criterion: Statement ("Every Anchor surface that shows spend (project rollups, effort metrics, session details)") + criterion 6
findings.message: The Statement names three surfaces: project rollups, EFFORT METRICS, session details. Phase 2 explicitly defers "Per-effort fleet-attribution ROLLUP/QUERY itself — schema-ready now, query surface deferred to a future effort." Yet Phase 3's unwrapped-sub-agent walk-through promises the opposite: "rollups sum child rows into the effort/fleet totals with the backfill provenance visible." Which is it? Either child rows ARE summed into an effort total (then the per-effort query exists this effort and Phase 2's deferral is wrong), or the query is deferred (then Phase 3's promise is unbacked and swarm spend is NOT visible at the effort level — the exact surface a frustrated user looks at after a fleet run: "what did that effort cost me?"). As written, the user's most natural question has no named owner: Phase 5 delivers per-lane + general PROJECT lines only. The existing `effort_view.effort_rollup` surface (which shows per-effort Σtok·time·$ today) is also an enumerated rollup consumer that criterion 6's honest counting must touch — the plan greps for consumers in Phase 5 but never states whether effort tiles gain the measured/child-row numbers or keep showing zeros for swarm-heavy efforts. Resolve the contradiction explicitly and name which phase makes effort metrics true.

findings.criterion: criteria 2 and 3 — surfaces must render honestly-provenanced states, and the deferral machinery is user-visible
findings.message: The frustrated-UX walk: a user closes a session while the service is mid-restart, the finalize defers, and the rollup now shows… what? The plan stamps "the triggering predicate reason on every deferred/skipped record" and surfaces "a `finalize-deferred` count on the rollup" — a bare count. No named surface renders the REASON, the expected resolution ("retried automatically by the ~30-min sweep"), or the time-to-terminal. The user sees "3 deferred" for up to ~10 hours with no way to know whether that is self-healing or stuck — precisely the trained-to-ignore-the-banner hazard the locked healthcheck-severity rule exists to prevent. Worse, the healthcheck WARN threshold is unspecified ("when live-registry sessions accumulate deferrals" — accumulate past WHAT?), so the one attention mechanism is undefined. And after `DEFER_RETRY_MAX` exhaustion the record silently becomes terminal `unmeasured` with the reason stamped on the record — again with no named surface showing the user that a session's spend was permanently given up and why. Specify: (a) the WARN threshold number, (b) which surface (session detail? rollup tooltip? `rnd spend`?) renders deferral reason + retry status + exhaustion outcome. Otherwise criterion 3's machinery is honest in the data layer and opaque at every surface the user actually reads.

findings.criterion: criteria 1 and 2 — swarm records must be visible on rendering surfaces
findings.message: The sweep mints child records with `session_id: sidecar:<engine-uuid>`. On every surface that lists sessions (project window tiles, `rnd spend`, coverage report), that renders as an opaque UUID string with no label, no skill, no narration — a wall of `sidecar:a3f9…` rows for a 20-agent fleet. The walk-through specifies attribution mechanics thoroughly but never the display contract: are child rows rolled up under the parent's tile (recommended — "S + 5 sub-agents: 14.2M tok"), listed as first-class rows, or hidden behind an expander? A fleet-heavy project could show dozens of unlabeled synthetic rows, burying the real sessions — the exact clutter problem the v7 "most-recent prominent, older under an expander" pattern was built to avoid. Name the render rule in Phase 5.

The backfill "REFUSES to run while the service is reachable unless `--force`." So the documented happy path for recovering history is: stop the Anchor service (dashboard goes dark), run a CLI, restart. Yet the plan's own trust-model row argues the tool is safe BY CONSTRUCTION regardless: exclusive-create claims cannot displace live records, terminal-status sessions only, snapshot-only reads. If the by-construction argument is sound, the service-down requirement is redundant ceremony that turns a one-command recovery into a service outage plus an elevated restart; if it is NOT sound, the trust-model row is overstated and `--force` (which re-enables the exact concurrent scenario) is under-guarded. Pick one: either drop the reachability refusal (keep the confirm flag) and let the CAS do its job, or state the concrete race the refusal prevents — "defense in depth" alone doesn't justify making the user take their own dashboard down, and in practice guarantees the recovery gets run with `--force` anyway, normalizing the override.

findings.criterion: criterion 3 — the hermetic predicate's closure claim
findings.message: The seam list is declared CLOSED: `ANCHOR_DATA_DIR`, `ANCHOR_SIDECAR_DIR`, `ANCHOR_WORKTREE_BASE`, `ANCHOR_SKILLS_DIR`, `ANCHOR_HEALTHCHECK`, `ANCHOR_PTY_BACKEND=stub`, `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD`, pytest-detection. But the healthcheck's own documented v4 walk also forces `ANCHOR_TERMINAL_SEED`, and the v8 test substrate forces `ANCHOR_GH_CMD` — both known hermetic markers absent from a list whose whole point is that closure is exhaustive. In practice any hermetic context also sets a listed seam, so this is defense-in-depth rather than a live hole — but a "CLOSED" list that misses known members on day one undermines the amendment discipline it's meant to establish (and the parametrized test will pass while the closure claim is already false). Sweep the codebase for every `ANCHOR_*` override at plan time and enumerate them all, or soften the closure claim to "the load-bearing subset."
